guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting against Miami simply because its latest result was extreme. Miami set program records with 856 total yards and 42 first downs against Florida A&M, while tying its scoring record with 77 points. That performance helps explain the market’s confidence, but our view is that one dominant result should not automatically be carried forward into the level of separation now required. For us, the case for Central Michigan is less about questioning which team is stronger and more about whether Miami’s recent ceiling is being priced too aggressively.

We also see more underlying transition than the early results suggest. Four of Miami’s five offensive-line starters from 2025 departed for the NFL, while both starting edge defenders became first-round draft selections. Those losses do not erase what Miami has done, but they add uncertainty when the market is demanding an unusually wide margin.

The meaningful concern for us is Central Michigan’s ability to create scoring opportunities. Our matchup numbers favor Miami heavily in that area, and Miami’s opponents have averaged only 3.6 yards per play while converting 21 percent of their third downs through two games. We still support Central Michigan at the available price, but its offense must avoid extended stretches of empty possessions to keep Miami from creating the separation the market expects.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Central Michigan’s offense against Miami’s scoring-opportunity prevention. Miami has already shown it can end drives quickly, holding Florida A&M’s offense to 107 total yards, four first downs and one third-down conversion in 14 attempts. Central Michigan does not need to match Miami’s offensive output for our position to work, but we think a few sustained drives could materially change the margin by limiting short fields and reducing Miami’s total possessions.

recent_game.fact: Miami improved to 2-0 with a 77-7 home win over Florida A&M on Sept. 10, 2026.
Miami set a program record with 856 total yards and an ACC record with 42 first downs against Florida A&M; its 77 points tied the program record.
Miami rushed for 430 yards, passed for 426 yards and averaged 11.7 yards per play against Florida A&M.
Miami scored on 11 of its first 12 possessions against Florida A&M.
Miami held Florida A&M's offense to 107 total yards, four first downs and a 1-for-14 third-down conversion rate; Florida A&M's only score was a 72-yard fumble return.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Darian Mensah completed 14 of 15 passes for 252 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions against Florida A&M.
Through two games, Mensah had completed 41 of 45 passes for 653 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions.
Mensah transferred to Miami from Duke in January 2026 after starting 14 games for Duke in 2025 and passing for 3,973 yards, 34 touchdowns and six interceptions.
Backup quarterback Luke Nickel completed all eight of his passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in his first major career action against Florida A&M.

offensive_personnel.fact: Miami used the same offensive-line starters in each of its first two games: Samson Okunlola at left tackle, SJ Alofaituli at left guard, Ryan Rodriguez at center, Max Buchanan at right guard and Matthew McCoy at right tackle.
Four of Miami's five 2025 offensive-line starters departed for the NFL, including drafted tackles Francis Mauigoa and Markel Bell and guard Anez Cooper.
Freshman running back Javian Mallory rushed for 142 yards and two touchdowns on 10 carries against Florida A&M, including a 52-yard touchdown run.
Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. rushed for 105 yards against Florida A&M and entered the next game with 2,458 career rushing yards, sixth in Miami history.
Wide receiver Malachi Toney followed his program-record 234-yard, three-touchdown performance at Stanford with four catches for 96 yards and one touchdown against Florida A&M.
Wide receiver Cooper Barkate transferred from Duke after catching 72 passes for 1,106 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025; he previously played with Mensah at Duke.

defensive_personnel.fact: Miami lost 2025 starting edge defenders Rueben Bain Jr. and Akheem Mesidor as first-round selections in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Miami returned defensive tackles Ahmad Moten Sr. and Justin Scott, who started the 2025 national championship game.
Miami added edge defender Damon Wilson II from Missouri after he started all 13 games, recorded nine sacks and earned second-team All-SEC honors in 2025.
Linebacker Mohamed Toure started all 16 games in 2025 and led Miami with 84 tackles.
Defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald recorded six interceptions in 2025, tying for second nationally and leading Miami and the ACC.

Miami changed three defensive starters from the Stanford opener to the Florida A&M game: Kamal Bonner replaced Chase Smith at linebacker, JJ Dunnigan replaced Bryce Fitzgerald at one safety spot, and Damari Brown replaced Xavier Lucas at cornerback.

coaching_changes.fact: Miami's 2026 coordinators are offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Shannon Dawson and defensive coordinator and linebackers coach Corey Hetherman; Jason Taylor is co-defensive coordinator and defensive-line coach.
Hetherman joined Miami in January 2025 after serving as Minnesota's defensive coordinator in 2024.

injury_availability.fact: Defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. missed 2026 spring football while recovering from an injury sustained in 2025, then started Miami's first two games of the 2026 season.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Miami averaged 61.0 points, 275.5 rushing yards and 427.0 passing yards per game while averaging 10.0 yards per play.
Miami converted 64 percent of its third downs and scored touchdowns on eight of 10 red-zone possessions through two games.
Miami returned 97.9 percent of its 2025 rushing production, including its top six rushers from that season.

defensive_context.fact: Miami allowed 6.5 points, 57.5 rushing yards and 145.5 passing yards per game through its first two contests.
Opponents averaged 3.6 yards per play and converted 21 percent of their third downs against Miami through two games.

In Hetherman's first season as defensive coordinator, Miami improved its scoring defense from 25.3 points per game in 2024 to 14.8 in 2025 and ranked first in the ACC in total, scoring and rushing defense.

special_teams.fact: Jake Weinberg made all seven extra points and a 46-yard field goal in the season opener at Stanford, then made Miami's first five extra points against Florida A&M.

other_relevant.fact: At the time of publication, Miami was 2-0 overall and had outscored Stanford and Florida A&M by a combined 122-13.
